thread.title: EUROPE MARKETS: Stoxx Europe 600 Edges Higher, Shaking Off Sweden's Election Results

author: morningstar.com
title: EUROPE MARKETS: Stoxx Europe 600 Edges Higher, Shaking Off Sweden's Election Results
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
RPC Group's stock soars on news of takeover talks
European stocks inched up Monday, as investors assessed ongoing worries over global trade while also weighing a win for anti-establishment politicians in Sweden's election.
What are markets doing?
The Stoxx Europe 600 rose 0.3% to 374.86, after inching higher in Friday's session but still suffering a weekly loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/europes-stock-index-slumps-on-track-for-worst-week-in-about-5-months-2018-09-07), as it dropped 2.2% last week.
The pan-European gauge is showing a decline of 3.7% for the year to date.
Germany's DAX 30 was higher by less than 0.1% to 11,963.36, while France's CAC 40 added 0.1% to 5,258.78. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 gained 0.1% to 7,285.98.
The euro edged up to $1.1564, up from $1.1553 late Friday in New York, while the pound bought $1.2942, up from $1.2901.
Don't miss:5 reasons to dial back on eurozone stocks for the rest of the year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/5-reasons-to-dial-back-on-eurozone-stocks-for-the-rest-of-the-year-2018-09-07)
What is driving the market?
Trade tensions between the U.S. and its partners have put pressure on global markets in recent months. A concern as the week kicks off is President Donald Trump's tweet over the weekend urging Apple Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-urges-apple-to-move-manufacturing-to-the-us-2018-09-08).(AAPL) to move its manufacturing to the U.S., a comment that helped put some pressure on Asian tech stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-stocks-dip-after-trumps-apple-production-comments-2018-09-09).
Investors also are worried about a fresh advance for anti-establishment European politicians, with Sweden becoming the latest country to show a shift over the weekend. The far-right Sweden Democrats, an anti-immigration party with roots in neo-Nazism, garnered an estimated 17.6% of ballots cast in Sunday's election (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/no-clear-majority-as-far-right-party-gains-in-sweden-election-2018-09-09).
What are strategists saying?
"The SD ran on a stricter immigration policy and want Sweden to leave the EU," said David Madden, a CMC Markets UK analyst, in a note, referring to the European Union, the region's big trade bloc.
"The election is unlikely to rock the financial markets, but growing euro-skepticism can't be ignored."
Stock movers
Shares in RPC Group PLC (RPC.LN) soared 21% after the packaging and containers company confirmed it's in talks to sell itself (http://admin.marketwatch.com/Newswire/Story/Story/ee09b1a5-b18e-420d-b187-71d0398c0f6d).
Shares in Compagnie Financiere Richemont SA (CFR.EB) tacked on 1.4% after the Cartier parent named Jerome Lambert as its CEO (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/richemont-names-new-ceo-sales-jump-2018-09-10). Richemont also said five-month sales through August showed double-digit percentage growth.
